items: Switch from bar soap to liquid body wash or shower gel because bar soap combines with water minerals to create sticky soap scum that coats pipe walls and causes slow drainage.
Use liquid soap products exclusively in all bathroom routines to prevent the mineral-soap reaction that causes residue to build up inside pipes over time.
Understand that switching soap types breaks the ongoing cycle of residue accumulation even though existing buildup requires separate treatment to remove completely.
Commit to liquid soap as a permanent change because enzymatic cleaners work most effectively when soap scum is not constantly being reintroduced into the system.
Install a hair catcher on every bathroom drain immediately because hair combined with soap residue is the primary cause of bathroom drain clogs according to professional plumbers.
Choose the right hair catcher style for each drain by using a tub stopper for showers and a flat stainless steel mesh screen for sinks to maximize effectiveness.
Clean your hair catcher every 2-3 showers or at least weekly by lifting it and removing all visible hair before rinsing it thoroughly under hot water.
Replace cheap plastic catchers with large holes because if water pools on top instead of draining, hair is still passing through and entering your pipes.
Use a drain snake to remove existing clogs before starting any prevention routine because enzymatic cleaners cannot dissolve solid blockages quickly enough to restore flow.
Apply 2 tablespoons of enzymatic drain cleaner into each bathroom drain monthly because these products digest organic buildup that causes slow drainage and future clogs.
Allow enzymatic cleaner to sit in the drain overnight for 8-12 hours without using it so the bacteria can fully break down residue inside the pipes.
Flush each drain with very hot water for 2 minutes the morning after treatment to wash away the loosened soap scum and debris dislodged by the cleaner.
categories: Clear Clogs and Maintain Drains Monthly
